body:
`insight:india-valuation-forward-returns` | confidence: **verified** | tags: india, base-rate, valuation

Nifty trailing P/E: a Stable Investor study (data to 2015) found that from P/E above 24, average subsequent 3/5/7-year returns were -5.1%/2.7%/9.9% a year, while from P/E below 12 the 5-year return averaged ~29% a year. Freefincal found every instance of a negative 5-year Nifty return started from P/E >=24.5, though over 3 years P/E was a weak predictor (negative 3-year returns from P/E >=22 only ~43% of the time). MoneyWorks4Me: entry above 22-25x led to poor 3-5 year returns, with the effect fading over 10-15 years. Sensex peaks: ~28x (2000) and ~27-28x (Jan 2008) both preceded ~60% crashes; troughs at ~12x (2008-09) preceded strong multi-year gains. Market cap/GDP: near 150% (2007) preceded roughly zero Sensex returns from Jan 2008 to late 2013; ~56% (Mar 2020) preceded a doubling within a year; 115-122% (2021) preceded a flat 2022; ~140% (mid-2024, a 15-year high) preceded the 2024-25 correction. Long-run average Sensex P/E ~18.5-19x; long-run mcap/GDP average ~76-81% (figures vary by GDP base). Caveats: index composition (more financials, fewer commodities) and lower rates may lift 'normal' P/Es; earnings-cycle troughs inflate P/E (Mar 2020). Rule: above ~24x trailing Nifty P/E or >~120% mcap/GDP, expect low single-digit 5-year returns; below ~14-15x or <~70%, expect high returns.

1. Survivorship mattered most for pledge: the survivors-only test said pledge flagged *more* multibaggers; with dead
   companies in, it is the one mechanical rule that clears the bar. This settles the conflict between Part A
   (8/20 traps vs 2/13 winners) and the old Part B in Part A's favour.
2. The cash-flow and balance-sheet "tells" (CFO/PAT, debt + negative CFO, other income, debtor days) stay questions.
   Two have point lifts near 1.5–2 but wide CIs and costs of 11–19% of winners. The v2 decision to make them deep-dive
   questions is confirmed, now on survivorship-free data.
3. Pledge is partly a leverage signal (60% overlap with weak interest cover), so pledge and the solvency flags should be
   read together, not added up as independent votes.
